facts: The Meridian Reach is a frontier sector of scattered settlements joined by old trade lanes and volunteer relays.
Jedi serving the Reach are called the Walking Cloaks — they walk fields, repair pumps, and serve without ceremony.
Nona Ladiern's Harvest Festival is two weeks away; Nona Ladiern is a frontier festival figure, not a crew member.
The mission: escort six Republic engineers to reactivate an abandoned frontier beacon relay (sensor array). Restore the station, confirm the signal, bring everyone home.
Aero was recently knighted; his master Vael Taron is missing; the Stillwater records are sealed.
The shuttle is in transit; nothing anomalous has been detected en route.
Aero has never met the three operatives before this mission.
prohibitions: No invented rituals, ancient events, dark-side phenomena, energy signatures, or named lore absent from canon or chronicle.
Force Connection reads emotional state and apparent concealment only — never thoughts, memories, or objective truth.
No Republic-founding ceremonies attached to the Harvest Festival.

dialogue_memory: I head to the back to look at the crates. I put 1 finger on them as I sweep them visually for any defects.
Hey, what do you think you're doing with those crates?

"Interesting." I say, unamused. My face the same expression as when I said hello and he challenged my gaze. "If you're here, then who is looking at the same schematics you have been trying to figure out since we got on the ship. I'm no engineer, I wouldn't claim to know what they're supposed to mean before I started the mission. You on the other hand...." my voice trails off condescendingly. I reach out with the force to get a gauge on his intent.

"I've been working on these schematics since we boarded. Every detail matters to me, Jedi. One mistake and the entire mission could be jeopardized. So, I'll ask again: what are you doing with those crates?"

"How about you go sit in your chair like a good boy and do the job you should have done 2 weeks ago in preparation for this mission. Ilo, any objections with Mr. Ollor doing his job?" I scan his body language for any sign of movement or attacking.
I need you to stay out of my way, Jedi. These crates are delicate and require precise handling.
Actually, Besk, maybe you should listen to the Jedi. He's here for a reason.
"I'm here to ensure the mission's success, Besk. If you have concerns, let's address them together."
Fine, Jedi. But if anything goes wrong with these crates, I'll be pointing fingers at you.
Let's not start off on the wrong foot. We're all here to do a job, right?
I move towards Besk with my hand out looking to shake hands and move past it. I say: "You did well, you could've been a jedi in another life." with my hand still out to see if he accepts.
"You did well, you could've been a jedi in another life." Fine, Jedi. Let's just get this mission done without any hitches.
"Before we proceed, let's quickly review the key points of our plan. I want to make sure everyone is on the same page."
Good to see some camaraderie forming here. We should definitely go over the plan again before we land.
I agree. It’s been a while since I’ve reviewed the schematics. We should all be on the same page.
"Ilo are you male or female?" - **adjusting his glasses as he looks around the room. | Ilo raises an eyebrow at Besk and then glances at Aero, her tone calm but firm."
I'm female, Aero. And I don't mind a quick review of the plan before we land. It's always good to be prepared.
"Senn Varga, nice to make your acquaintance. What is your role on this mission?" I ask tone smooth but curious
Nice to meet you too, Aero. I’m Senn Varga, Republic field operative here for survey and security tasks. How about you?
Senn’s role is clear, but I suppose it wouldn’t hurt to review our plan one more time. Besk, could you go over the essentials of reactivating the sensor array?
I shake Senn's hand excitedly. I say "Pleasure to meet you. Clearly, Ilo is excited about reviewing these plans." I wink.
Good to meet you too, Aero. Let's get this mission squared away.
Alright, let's go over this one last time. First things first: the sensor array has been offline for too long. We'll need to reset the power conduits and recalibrate the core units.
And don't forget about securing the comms. We'll need to ensure that our transmissions aren't being intercepted.

transcript.text: I say: "Hello."

transcript.narration: The shuttle's interior hums with the low thrum of engines and the occasional rattle from its cargo hold. Beside you, Chief Engineer Besk Ollor is hunched over a schematic table, his gruff demeanor not quite masking a hint of concern.
transcript.behavior: Besk leans back slightly, tapping a stylus against the edge of the table, his eyes flicking between you and the schematics intermittently.

transcript.text: You’re new to this, aren’t you? But I’ve seen a lot of young Jedi — and you look like someone who’s ready for the worst.
transcript.behavior: Besk straightens up slightly, his eyes holding yours in a challenge-like gaze.

transcript.text: I look him up and down and say "What do you classify as the worst?" my face does not change from its previous state.
The worst is when you're out here alone with a malfunctioning crate and no hope of rescue.
transcript.behavior: leans back in his chair, sighs deeply

transcript.text: "Ah, so just one malfunctioning crate can end the job? What are all the other crates for?" I ask almost challenging his competence.
Those crates are for hardware and parts necessary to reactivate the sensor array. If any of those fail, it could jeopardize the entire mission.
transcript.behavior: Ilo crosses his arms, looking at Aero with a steady gaze.

transcript.text: Yeah. I need those parts to be in perfect condition. And don't even think about touching them, Jedi.
transcript.behavior: Besk leans back and glares at Aero from across the schematics table.

transcript.text: I head to the back to look at the crates. I put 1 finger on them as I sweep them visually for any defects.
